full_judgment:
2. Short facts are that the petitioner joined the then Pakistan Army and was commissioned as Second Lieutenant on 29-3-1970 and ultimately, was promoted as Captain in 1974. In 1979 he was deputed as Director of Central Transport Pool of the Bangladesh Secretariat Service. The service of the petitioner was placed under the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources on 3-3-1980 for appointment on deputation as Manager of respondent No. 2 i.e. Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited. The Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources was renamed as Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources and the said Ministry appointed the petitioner as officer on special duty in the Petro-Bangla until further order by Memo dated 13-6-1985. It further appears that Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Resources Corporation appointed the petitioner as Senior Manager-in-Charge. By Memo dated 10-11-1986 of Chief Martial Law Administrator's office the petitioner was retired from Bangladesh Army with direction to reappoint him in the civil post held by him as a permanent incumbent. By memo dated 6-6-1987, the petitioner was absorbed as Manager (Transport) of respondent No. 2 with effect from 1-1-1987. It was mentioned in the said memo that service condition of the petitioner would be ignored by regulations framed for the employees of respondent No. 1 as per above memo: It is clear from the said memo the petitioner was absorbed as an employee of respondent No. 1 and deputed as Manager (Transport) of respondent No. 2 which is a subsidiary company of respondent No. 1. The petitioner was appointed as Senior Manager-in-Charge of Services Department of respondent No. 2. The respondent No. 1 by order dated 11-2-1988 transferred the petitioner to Compressed Natural Gas Company Limited a subsidiary company of respondent No. 1 as Manager (Administration and Logistics). Again he was transferred by order dated 28-11-1989 to the office of respondent No. 2 to act as Manager (Administration). Then he was again transferred to Bakhrabad Gas Systems Limited by order dated 5-5-1992 as Deputy General Manager. The petitioner was again transferred to respondent No. 2 by respondent No. 1 as General Manager-in-Charge (Administration) where he joined and his joining report was accepted by order dated 25-7-1995. While he was on leave, the respondent No. 2 by order dated 20-9-1995 prematurely retired the petitioner from service in exercise of alleged power under Rule 5(Kha) of the Pension and General Provident Fund Rules, 1987, although the petitioner will attain normal age of superannuation in 2005 on completion of 57 years of age. Being aggrieved by order of retirement the petitioner made representation to the respondent No. 1 on 23-9-95 which was turned down and thereafter, the petitioner moved the High Court Division in the present writ petition and obtained the Rule. 

 3. The respondent Nos. 1-2 contested the Rule by filing joint affidavit-in-opposition and denied the material allegations. They contended, inter alia, that the petitioner was commissioned in the Army on 29-3-1970 and retired from the Army on 31-12-1986 and this period was on his own request computed with his service under respondent No. 2 for the purpose of pension from respondent No. 2. On the date of his retirement the petitioner completed more than 25 years of service and the authority in the interest of the company retired him on 20-9-1995 from service with pension under rule 5(Kha) of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution-Company Limited Pension and General Provident Fund Rules, 1987. Rule 5(Kha) of the aforesaid Rules confers power on the Company to retire an employee from the service on completion of 25 years of his service in the interest of the company and the company is not required to assign any reason for such retirement. It was further contended that the petitioner was in the service of Bangladesh Army up to 31-12-1986. Thereafter he was serving on deputation under respondent No. 1 as Senior Manager (Service) and then he joined the service of the respondent No. 2 as Manager (Personnel) on 3-3-1980. As per direction contained in Annexure-D to the writ petition, the respondent No. 1 could not appoint the petitioner in the post of Senior Manager under respondent No. 1 and with the sanction of the Ministry absorbed him in the service of the respondent No. 2 as Manager (Transport) with effect from 1-1-1987. It is clear from Annexure-E that respondent No. 1 as the controlling Corporation of the respondent No. 2 appointed/absorbed the petitioner as an employee of respondent No. 2. It is also clear from Annexure-G and H that the petitioner was an employee of respondent No 2 and not respondent No. 1 Further there, Annexure-J to the writ petition (representation dated 24-4-95 for promotion made to respondent No. 1) the petitioner described himself as Deputy General Manager of respondent No. 2, On deputation in the Bakhrabad Gas Systems Limited. The petitioner thus being an employee of respondent No. 2 the pension rules are applicable to him specially because the petitioner himself requested respondent No. 2 to accept him as a beneficiary of the said Pension Rules through an application dated 16-3-92. In that view of the matter; the question of applicability of the Service Regulations of respondent No. 1 to the petitioner does not arise. 

 4. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 by filing supplementary affidavit brought on record certain materials relevant for appreciation of the issues involved in the writ petition. Annexure 17, resolution of Board meeting of the corporation held on 22-4-89 shows that in its 80th Board meeting the Corporation took certain decisions namely, (1) the corporation will appoint Chief Executive of the Company and they will be officers of the Corporation. Their service will be regulated by the Corporation's Service Rules (2). All officers of the Company including the General Manager and other equivalent posts will be placed under administrative control of the company and (3) the Board will take decision in this regard in its monthly Meeting to be held on 23-4-89. The corporation in its 97th Board Meeting held on 14-11-89 prepared a list of officers and employees who have exercised options as a follow up measure to implement its decision vide Annexure 20 in which the petitioner's name appeared at serial 39. 

 7. It is undisputed that the petitioner joined the then Pakistan Army in 1969 and was commissioned as 2nd Lieutenant on 29-3-1970 and he was later on promoted as Captain in 1974 and thereafter in 1970 he was deputed to the Bangladesh Secretariat Transport Pool and was appointed as Director of Central Transport Pool. By memo dated 3-8-1980, the service of the petitioner was placed under Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and he was appointed, on deputation as Manager of respondent No. 2. He was subsequently appointed officer on special duty, in the Petrobangla by memo dated 13-6-1985. The corporation also later on appointed as Senior Manager in Charge of Services Division and later on, by memo dated 10-11-1986 of the Chief Martial Law Administrator's Secretariat, the petitioner, was retired from Army service with direction to appoint him in civil post as permanent incumber it. Thereafter, on 6-6-1987, the petitioner was permanently absorbed in the corporation and the respondent N. 2, which is a subsidiary company of respondent No. 1. 

 8. The respondent No. 1 by order dated 11-3-89 transferred the petitioner to-Compressed Natural Gas Company Limited as Manager and again he was transferred by order dated 28-11-89 to the office of the respondent No. 2 to act as Manager (Administration). The petitioner was again transferred to Bhakrabad Gas Systems Limited of the respondent No. 1 by order dated 5-5-1992 as Deputy General Manager. The petitioner was again, transferred to respondent No. 2 by respondent No. 1. It is also undisputed that by order dated 20-5-1995, the petitioner was prematurely retired from the service, in exercise of power under Rule 5(Kha) of Pension and General Provident Fund Rules 1987. The petitioner will attain the age of superannuating in 2005 on completion of 57 years of age. 

 10. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that Titas Cas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited is an attached department of the Corporation and, as such the employee will be treated as employee of the corporation and not Of the company. In support of his contention, the learned counsel has placed before us the case 61 Mosharraf Hossain Chowdhury vs General Manager, Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Co Ltd another reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 61. He then cited the case of Bangladesh Birnan Corporation Government of Bangladesh and others; reported in 2000 BLD (AD) 230 and submitted that past service in the defence service counts towards seniority on appointment in civil post. A Birnan employee is public servant within the meaning of section 2(d) of the Public Servants (Retirement) Act, 1974. A defence Service Officer appointed in the service of the Birnan Corporation falls within the category of public servant to whom the Public Servants (Retireinent) Act, 1974 is equally applicable.
